subject.title: Managed (non-hot-reloadable) policy tier: config writes currently disable every protection layer

question: Should OpenClaw support an OS-admin-enforced policy tier that overrides the current trusted-user configuration model?
rationale: Current policy deliberately treats configuration writers and authenticated control-plane callers as trusted operators, so adding a non-overridable tier changes the supported security boundary and requires explicit cross-platform product semantics.

options.title: Sponsor managed policy design
options.body: Add a core admin-owned policy source with canonical precedence, ownership checks, write-path enforcement, diagnostics, and restart semantics.

options.title: Keep single-operator boundary
options.body: Retain the current contract and strengthen deployment guidance around separate OS identities, gateways, and externally protected state directories.

recommendation.title: Sponsor managed policy design
recommendation.body: Add a core admin-owned policy source with canonical precedence, ownership checks, write-path enforcement, diagnostics, and restart semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to both the normative security trust model and the configuration recovery and reload contract.
